Ali Hoca iyi niyetli ve öğrenci dostu bir insan fakat bu dersi bu kadar slayttan ve MATLAB kodlaması üzerinden işlemesine rağmen sınıfta ve assignmentlarda benzerini çözmediğimiz türde uzun sınav soruları sorması garibime gitti açıkçası. Bu tercih her ne kadar ders saati imitasyonu göz önünde bulundurulduğunda mantıklı olsa da bazı assignmentlar 10-15 saat hatta belki daha fazla zaman alacak derecede ayarsız zorlayıcıydı. Bunlara ek olarak, hocanın slaytlarının bazılarını NotebookLM'e yaptırması geri kalanını da textbook'tan belli kesitleri screenshot alarak copy paste yapması slaytları kullanarak çalışmayı zor bir hale getirdi.

In my opinion, it doesn't make sense to give a 3-hour exam where solving even a single question takes more than 3 hours, especially when the questions have very little to do with the methods taught in class, and despite the instructor only teaching the methods themselves without solving any example problems or providing any study materials.

In a 3-hour, 3-question exam, when solving for ICI is already hard enough, asking for IQI as an extra is completely illogical for an exam solved by hand on paper.

Furthermore, in another question involving a complex connection of 5 springs where 2 of the spring constants are non-linear, making us derive a complex equation with 3 unknowns from this spring system, then take the partial derivatives of this equation with respect to 3 different variables, and finally take the second partial derivatives of those initial partial derivatives with respect to each variable—all on a pen-and-paper exam—is again completely illogical. Not to mention, expecting us to solve this main equation using penalty methods is a whole other issue.

In yet another question, asking something that might be easy to solve, but providing absolutely zero information in class about its logic and without showing even a basic example of how to derive it, and just saying "go derive the 4-point forward Euler formula" during the exam proves that the purpose of the exam is not to teach, but simply an attempt to force a low class average.

Also, the professor urgently needs to deeply rethink what "easy" means and change the definition in his brain.

The grading system of the course is quite problematic. Considering that the quizzes contribute 5% to the overall grade, I don’t think there’s a need for so many quizzes. The total contribution of quizzes  exceed that of two midterms and a final. This situation places a mental burden on us as students because we inevitably approach the quizzes with the seriousness of a midterm. Moreover, despite their importance, cheating during quizzes cannot be effectively prevented. Even though our professor is aware of the issue, no effective measures have been taken. On top of that, homework questions—whose solutions are accessible for everyone—were used in quizzes for both sections. This was unfair to those of us who took the quiz before the other section, as they had access to the answers beforehand. Additionally, the idea of awarding points for attendance, which was implemented for the first time this year, has brought everyone’s grades closer together, which will likely lead to grade clustering and very small differences causing significant impacts on letter grades. Finally, I believe the way exams are graded is also problematic. Marks are assigned without any annotations or clear criteria on the papers. Strangely enough, the average for each exam ends up within a similar range. I think the exams should be graded using an answer key shared with us, as is done for the quizzes. This would ensure greater transparency. The only positive aspect of the course is that our professor is very organized.
